note: Rescored against dataset v2.1 labels from the first-run per-query retrieved_docs stored in article_01_benchmarks_corrected_2026-10-04.json. Recall@5 and MRR use BenchmarkRunner._calculate_recall_at_k and _calculate_mrr. Values are single-run. The HyDE, decomposition and composite configurations could not be rerun on their original generator: the fallback chain started with Groq llama-3.1-8b-instant, which Groq retired on 2026-10-05. Validation: rebuilding the naive index retrieval-only under the original checkout path and collection name reproduced the stored naive retrieved_docs for all 142 questions.
environment_notes: The naive Chroma index was built from the original corpus. The in-memory index shared by dense_inmemory, hyde, decomposition and hyde_decomposition was built after datasets/tech_docs/attribution.md had been edited with a provenance note (since moved to datasets/CORPUS_PROVENANCE.md). Those four configurations are like-for-like with each other; naive is not like-for-like with them.

Both pipelines embed the absolute file_path of each document with every chunk, and the naive pipeline also embeds the source path and the Chroma collection name. Retrieval results therefore depend on the checkout location and the collection name. Measured: naive Recall@5 0.847 from the original checkout versus 0.822 from another path; dense_inmemory 0.838 versus 0.825.
Latency is copied from the 2026-10-04 three-run execution over the 150-question v2.0 set. dense_inmemory latency comes from a separate execution and is not comparable with the other rows.
